sentences.en: The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy is astonishing - Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for $13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn't have any physical product at all.
sentences.cn: 数字经济巨头们的实力与野心令人震惊——亚马逊刚刚宣布以 135 亿美元收购高端连锁杂货店全食超市，但两年前 Facebook 收购 WhatsApp 即时通讯服务所支付的费用甚至比这还要高，而后者根本没有任何实体产品。

sentences.en: What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives.
sentences.cn: WhatsApp 提供给 Facebook 的，是一张错综复杂、细致入微的用户友谊与社交生活之网。

sentences.en: Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through.
sentences.cn: Facebook 当时向欧委会承诺不会把电话号码与 Facebook 身份关联，但协议刚获准通过，它就背弃了这一承诺。

sentences.en: Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be.
sentences.cn: 即使不了解信息的具体内容，但其发送者以及接收者的（身份）信息在极大程度上也会透露内情，且这种情况仍会继续。

sentences.en: What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting?
sentences.cn: 特蕾莎·梅的政敌正在其中进行密谋的那些 WhatsApp（聊天）群，哪个政治记者、哪个党鞭会不想了解其构成呢？

sentences.en: It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what.
sentences.cn: 亚马逊之所以看重全食超市，其价值与其说是在于它旗下的 460 间店铺，倒不如说在于其顾客的购买记录。

sentences.en: Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power.
sentences.cn: 竞争法似乎是解决这些权力失衡问题的唯一办法。

sentences.en: But it is clumsy.
sentences.cn: 但它却笨拙不堪。

sentences.en: For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy.
sentences.cn: 一方面，相较于数字经济中革新的步伐，它太慢了。

sentences.en: By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power.
sentences.cn: 某个问题待其得到解决和补救时，这个问题可能已经在市场中蒸发不见了，取而代之的是新的权力滥用。

sentences.en: But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too.
sentences.cn: 但是还存在一个更深层的概念性问题。

sentences.en: Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them.
sentences.cn: 当前所阐释的竞争法应对的是消费者的经济损失问题，而当这些服务的用户并不是它们的支付者时，法规就不明确了。

sentences.en: The users of their services are not their customers.
sentences.cn: 其（数字巨头）服务的用户不是它们的顾客。

sentences.en: That would be the people who buy advertising from them - and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies.
sentences.cn: 它们的顾客是那些花钱购买广告的人——而 Facebook 和谷歌这两大虚拟巨头掌控了数字广告，这不利于所有其他的媒体和娱乐公司。

sentences.en: The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants.
sentences.cn: 它们售卖的产品是数据，而我们这些用户，将我们的生活转化为数据，为数字巨头盈利之用。

sentences.en: Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield.
sentences.cn: 就好像有些蚂蚁会养殖一种名为蚜虫的昆虫，以获取它们进食时分泌出的蜜露，同样地，Google 养殖我们是为了获取我们数字生活所产生的数据。

sentences.en: Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes.
sentences.cn: 蚂蚁防范食肉昆虫靠近其蚜虫进食之处；Gmail 防范垃圾邮件发送者入侵我们的收件箱。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.
sentences.cn: 这可不像一种人类的、或者说民主的关系，尽管双方均能够获益。

sentences.en: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" - the ability to focus without distraction.
sentences.cn: 为避免陷入“高度重视忙碌”的陷阱，《深度工作：在一个让人分心的世界，集中精力取得成功的法则》一书作者卡尔·纽坡特，建议打造“深度工作”的习惯——即集中注意力、不分心的能力。

sentences.en: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work - be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day.
sentences.cn: 掌握深度工作艺术的方法有很多——或是长久隐退、专注于某一特定工作；或是形成一种日常惯例；或是采取“新闻工作者”的方法，抓住一天中能抓住的深度工作时刻。

sentences.en: Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
sentences.cn: 无论哪种方式，关键都是：确定你的专注时长并坚持下去。

sentences.en: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time.
sentences.cn: 纽坡特还建议“深度规划”以对抗持续干扰并在更短的时间内完成更多的工作。

sentences.en: "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month.
sentences.cn: “在任何特定时刻，我都会为接下来的大约一个月制定深度工作计划。

sentences.en: Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.
sentences.cn: 一旦落于日程表，我就会一如守护就诊预约或重要会议安排一样守护这一时间安排”，他写道。

sentences.en: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day - in particular how we craft our to-do lists.
sentences.cn: 另一项实现事半功倍之策就是反思“你是怎样安排你的一天的”——特别是，我们是怎样精心制作任务清单的。

sentences.en: Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.
sentences.cn: 提姆·哈福德，《混乱：改变我们生活的无序力量》的作者，提到了 20 世纪 80 年代初的一项研究：该研究将本科生分为两组，一些被建议设定每月的目标及学习活动；另一些人被要求逐日地、更详细地计划活动及目标。

sentences.en: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students.
sentences.cn: 虽然研究者假设井井有条的每日计划对于任务执行会非常有效，但是他们错了：详尽的每日计划使学生受挫。

sentences.en: Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.
sentences.cn: 哈福德提出，无可避免的干扰通常会使每日任务清单失效，而在任务清单中留出临时应变的空间则能收获最佳结果。

sentences.en: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".
sentences.cn: 若要充分利用自身专注力以及精力，我们还需要“拥抱闲暇时间”，或如纽坡特所建议的，“偷偷懒”。

sentences.en: "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body ... [idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.
sentences.cn: “闲散不仅仅是一次假期、一种放纵或一个恶习；它之于大脑就像维他命 D 之于身体一样不可或缺……矛盾的是，它对于完成任何工作都不可或缺”，他提出。

sentences.en: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate.
sentences.cn: 斯利尼·皮莱，哈佛医学院的一位精神病学助理教授，认为“闲暇时光”与“生产效率”之间有违直觉的联系可能源于我们大脑的运作方式。

sentences.en: When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
sentences.cn: 当我们的大脑就某项工作在“集中注意力”与“分散注意力”之间切换时，它们往往更高效。

sentences.en: "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.
sentences.cn: “人们没有意识到的是，要完成这些工作，他们需要使用‘专注’和‘分心’两种大脑回路”，皮莱说道。

sentences.en: Unlike so-called basic emotions such as sadness, fear, and anger, guilt emerges a little later, in conjunction with a child's growing grasp of social and moral norms.
sentences.cn: 与悲伤、恐惧和愤怒等所谓的基本情绪不同，内疚感出现得稍晚，它与孩子对社会及道德规范的逐渐领会相伴相生。

sentences.en: Children aren't born knowing how to say "I'm sorry"; rather, they learn over time that such statements appease parents and friends - and their own consciences.
sentences.cn: 孩子并非生来便知晓如何说“对不起”；而是随着时间的推移才逐渐明白这种表达可以安抚父母、朋友——以及自己的道德心。

sentences.en: This is why researchers generally regard so-called moral guilt, in the right amount, to be a good thing.
sentences.cn: 正因如此，研究者通常认为所谓的道德负疚感，如若适量，会是好事。

sentences.en: In the popular imagination, of course, guilt still gets a bad rap.
sentences.cn: 当然，在大众想象中内疚感可不是件好事。

sentences.en: It is deeply uncomfortable - it's the emotional equivalent of wearing a jacket weighted with stones.
sentences.cn: 它令人深感不安——它是“身负重甲的情感”。

sentences.en: Yet this understanding is outdated.
sentences.cn: 然而这种看法已经过时。

sentences.en: "There has been a kind of revival or a rethinking about what guilt is and what role guilt can serve," says Amrisha Vaish, a psychology researcher at the University of Virginia, adding that this revival is part of a larger recognition that emotions aren't binary - feelings that may be advantageous in one context may be harmful in another.
sentences.cn: “现在已再度兴起，或者说人们已开始重新思考内疚感到底是什么，又可以起到什么作用，”弗吉尼亚大学心理学研究者阿姆瑞沙·瓦依希说道，且补充指出，这种复兴属于一种更宏观认识的一部分，即，情绪并不是二元对立的（并不是非好即坏的；并非是只能二者择一的）——在一种情境下有利的情绪在另一情境下可能有害。

sentences.en: Jealousy and anger, for example, may have evolved to alert us to important inequalities.
sentences.cn: 例如，嫉妒和愤怒可能已经进化到能够提醒我们注意影响重大的不平等。

sentences.en: Too much happiness can be destructive.
sentences.cn: 而太过愉悦可能具有毁灭性。

sentences.en: And guilt, by prompting us to think more deeply about our goodness, can encourage humans to make up for errors and fix relationships.
sentences.cn: 而内疚感，通过刺激我们深入挖掘人性之善，可以鼓励人们弥补错误并修复关系。

sentences.en: Guilt, in other words, can help hold a cooperative species together.
sentences.cn: 换言之，内疚感有助于将一个合作性物种凝聚在一起。

sentences.en: It is a kind of social glue.
sentences.cn: 它是一种社会粘合剂。

sentences.en: Viewed in this light, guilt is an opportunity.
sentences.cn: 从这一角度来看，内疚感是一种机会。

sentences.en: Work by Tina Malti, a psychology professor at the University of Toronto, suggests that guilt may compensate for an emotional deficiency.
sentences.cn: 多伦多大学心理学教授蒂娜·马尔蒂的研究表明，内疚感可以弥补某种情感缺失。

sentences.en: In a number of studies, Malti and others have shown that guilt and sympathy may represent different pathways to cooperation and sharing.
sentences.cn: 马尔蒂等多次研究发现，内疚感和同情心可能代表着通往合作与分享的不同路径。

sentences.en: Some kids who are low in sympathy may make up for that shortfall by experiencing more guilt, which can rein in their nastier impulses.
sentences.cn: 同情心较低的孩子可以通过体验更多的内疚感来弥补这一不足，这种内疚感可以遏制他们的恶意冲动。

sentences.en: And vice versa: High sympathy can substitute for low guilt.
sentences.cn: 反之亦然：富有同情心可以替代缺乏内疚感。

sentences.en: In a 2014 study, for example, Malti looked at 244 children.
sentences.cn: 例如，在2014年的一项研究中，马尔蒂调查了244个孩子。

sentences.en: Using caregiver assessments and the children's self-observations, she rated each child's overall sympathy level and his or her tendency to feel negative emotions after moral transgressions.
sentences.cn: 根据看护人的评价和孩子的自我观察，她评估了每个孩子总体的同情心水平，以及他或她在道德越轨后产生负面情绪的倾向。

sentences.en: Then the kids were handed chocolate coins, and given a chance to share them with an anonymous child.
sentences.cn: 然后研究者分发给孩子们一些金币巧克力，并给他们一次与一个不知姓名的孩子分享巧克力的机会。

sentences.en: For the low-sympathy kids, how much they shared appeared to turn on how inclined they were to feel guilty.
sentences.cn: 对于那些缺乏同情心的孩子，他们分享出多少（巧克力）取决于他们感到内疚的倾向。

sentences.en: The guilt-prone ones shared more, even though they hadn't magically become more sympathetic to the other child's deprivation.
sentences.cn: 容易感到内疚的孩子会拿出更多分享，虽然他们并没有魔法般地变得更加同情对方的贫乏。

sentences.en: "That's good news, " Malti says.
sentences.cn: “这是好消息，”马尔蒂说。

sentences.en: "We can be prosocial because we caused harm and we feel regret."
sentences.cn: “我们可能会因为自己造成伤害并感到懊悔而变得亲社会。”

sentences.en: Forests give us shade, quiet and one of the harder challenges in the fight against climate change.
sentences.cn: 森林给我们带来了树阴和宁静，也给应对气候变化的战斗带来了一项更严峻的挑战。

sentences.en: Even as we humans count on forests to soak up a good share of the carbon dioxide we produce, we are threatening their ability to do so.
sentences.cn: 就在我们人类依靠森林来吸收我们所产生的相当一部分二氧化碳之时，我们也正在威胁它们的这一能力。

sentences.en: The climate change we are hastening could one day leave us with forests that emit more carbon than they absorb.
sentences.cn: 因人类而不断加剧的气候变化或许终有一天会留给我们碳排放量超过吸收量的森林。

sentences.en: Thankfully, there is a way out of this trap - but it involves striking a subtle balance.
sentences.cn: 值得庆幸的是，有一种方法可以摆脱这一困境——但这需要达成一种微妙的平衡。

sentences.en: Helping forests flourish as valuable "carbon sinks" long into the future may require reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now.
sentences.cn: 要促使森林发展成为宝贵的“碳汇”并一直持续下去，可能需要降低它们现有的碳吸收能力。

sentences.en: California is leading the way, as it does on so many climate efforts, in figuring out the details.
sentences.cn: 加州在明确细节方面做出了示范，正如它在诸多应对气候变化的运动中所做的一样。

sentences.en: The state's proposed Forest Carbon Plan aims to double efforts to thin out young trees and clear brush in parts of the forest.
sentences.cn: 该州提出的森林碳计划致力于在部分森林里加倍疏伐幼树、清除灌木的力度。

sentences.en: This temporarily lowers carbon-carrying capacity.
sentences.cn: 这会暂时降低碳容纳量。

sentences.en: But the remaining trees draw a greater share of the available moisture, so they grow and thrive, restoring the forest's capacity to pull carbon from the air.
sentences.cn: 但剩余的树木会吸收更多可用水分，从而茁壮成长，修复森林从空气中吸收碳的能力。

sentences.en: Healthy trees are also better able to fend off insects.
sentences.cn: 健康的树木还能更好地防御昆虫。

sentences.en: The landscape is rendered less easily burnable.
sentences.cn: 林地的易燃性会降低。

sentences.en: Even in the event of a fire, fewer trees are consumed.
sentences.cn: 即使发生火灾，烧毁的树木也更少。

sentences.en: The need for such planning is increasingly urgent.
sentences.cn: 对于这类计划的需求正变得越来越迫切。

sentences.en: Already, since 2010, drought and insects have killed over 100 million trees in California, most of them in 2016 alone, and wildfires have burned hundreds of thousands of acres.
sentences.cn: 干旱和昆虫自2010年起就已经导致加州1亿多棵树木死亡，其中绝大多数都发生在2016年短短一年间，野火已经烧毁了数十万英亩森林。

sentences.en: California plans to treat 35,000 acres of forest a year by 2020, and 60,000 by 2030 - financed from the proceeds of the state's emissions-permit auctions.
sentences.cn: 加州计划到2020年每年处理森林面积达到35000英亩，2030年则达到60000英亩——资金来源于该州（碳）排放许可证拍卖的收益。

sentences.en: That's only a small share of the total acreage that could benefit, about half a million acres in all, so it will be vital to prioritize areas at greatest risk of fire or drought.
sentences.cn: 这在总面积约50万英亩的可受益森林中仅占很小的比例，因此优先处理火灾或干旱风险最大的区域是至关重要的。

sentences.en: The strategy also aims to ensure that carbon in woody material removed from the forests is locked away in the form of solid lumber or burned as biofuel in vehicles that would otherwise run on fossil fuels.
sentences.cn: 该战略的另一目标是，确保从森林中移除的木本材料内的碳以固体木材的形式封存起来，或作为生物燃料供那些原本使用化石燃料的车辆使用。

sentences.en: New research on transportation biofuels is already under way.
sentences.cn: 关于交通用生物燃料的新研究已在进行中。

sentences.en: State governments are well accustomed to managing forests, but traditionally they've focused on wildlife, watersheds and opportunities for recreation.
sentences.cn: 各州政府对于森林管理已驾轻就熟，但他们历来都把重点放在野生动物、水域及重建机遇上。

sentences.en: Only recently have they come to see the vital part forests will have to play in storing carbon.
sentences.cn: 直到最近，他们才意识到必须让森林在碳储存方面发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.
sentences.cn: 加州计划——预计于明年由州长最终敲定——应该成为一个典范。

sentences.en: American farmers have been complaining of labor shortages for several years.
sentences.cn: 多年来，美国农户一直在抱怨劳动力短缺。

sentences.en: The complaints are unlikely to stop without an overhaul of immigration rules for farm workers.
sentences.cn: 如果不彻底改革农工移民政策，这些抱怨不大可能停止。

sentences.en: Congress has obstructed efforts to create a more straightforward visa for agricultural workers that would let foreign workers stay longer in the U.S. and change jobs within the industry.
sentences.cn: 美国国会一直在阻挠为农业工人创设一个更简易的签证以允许外籍劳工在美国停留更长时间并在行业内更换工作的努力。

sentences.en: If this doesn't change, American businesses, communities, and consumers will be the losers.
sentences.cn: 如果这种情况不发生改变，美国企业、社会各界以及消费者都将成为受害者。

sentences.en: Perhaps half of U.S. farm laborers are undocumented immigrants.
sentences.cn: 也许一半的美国农工属于非法移民。

sentences.en: As fewer such workers enter the country, the characteristics of the agricultural workforce are changing.
sentences.cn: 随着此类劳工赴美数量的减少，农业劳动力的特征也正在发生变化。

sentences.en: Today's farm laborers, while still predominantly born in Mexico, are more likely to be settled rather than migrating and more likely to be married than single.
sentences.cn: 今天的农工，虽然仍然主要出生在墨西哥，但更有可能是定居而非移居，更有可能是已婚而非单身。

sentences.en: They're also aging.
sentences.cn: 他们正在老龄化。

sentences.en: At the start of this century, about one-third of crop workers were over the age of 35.
sentences.cn: 本世纪初，大约三分之一的农作物工人年龄超35岁。

sentences.en: Now more than half are.
sentences.cn: 现在，超35岁者过半。

sentences.en: And picking crops is hard on older bodies.
sentences.cn: 而且，收割庄稼对年老的人而言很难。

sentences.en: One oft-debated cure for this labor shortage remains as implausible as it's been all along: Native U.S. workers won't be returning to the farm.
sentences.cn: 针对这一劳动力短缺的一个常被争论的解决办法仍然一如既往地不现实：美国本土工人不会回归农场。

sentences.en: Mechanization isn't the answer, either - not yet, at least.
sentences.cn: 机械化也不是解决办法，至少现在还不是。

sentences.en: Production of corn, cotton, rice, soybeans, and wheat has been largely mechanized, but many high-value, labor-intensive crops, such as strawberries, need labor.
sentences.cn: 玉米、棉花、水稻、大豆和小麦的生产已基本实现机械化，但许多高价值、劳动密集型农作物需要劳动力，比如草莓。

sentences.en: Even dairy farms, where robots do a small share of milking, have a long way to go before they're automated.
sentences.cn: 即使是机器人承担小部分挤奶工作的乳牛场，在实现自动化之前也还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: As a result, farms have grown increasingly reliant on temporary guest workers using the H-2A visa to fill the gaps in the workforce.
sentences.cn: 因此，农场越来越依赖于使用H-2A签证的临时外籍工人来填补劳动力缺口。

sentences.en: Starting around 2012, requests for the visas rose sharply; from 2011 to 2016 the number of visas issued more than doubled.
sentences.cn: 从2012年左右开始，申请此类签证的人数突然大幅上升；从2011年到2016年，签发的签证数量增加了一倍多。

sentences.en: The H-2A visa has no numerical cap, unlike the H-2B visa for nonagricultural work, which is limited to 66,000 a year.
sentences.cn: 与非农工H-2B签证（每年上限为6.6万个）不同，H-2A签证没有数量限制。

sentences.en: Even so, employers complain they aren't given all the workers they need.
sentences.cn: 即便如此，雇主仍抱怨未能获得足够劳工。

sentences.en: The process is cumbersome, expensive, and unreliable.
sentences.cn: 这个过程繁琐、昂贵且不可靠。

sentences.en: One survey found that bureaucratic delays led the average H-2A worker to arrive on the job 22 days late.
sentences.cn: 一项调查发现，官僚主义所致的迟滞使得H-2A签证工人的上工时间平均晚22天。

sentences.en: The shortage is compounded by federal immigration raids, which remove some workers and drive others underground.
sentences.cn: 联邦政府对移民的突击搜查也加剧了劳动力短缺，一些工人被驱逐出境，另一些则被迫转入地下。

sentences.en: In a 2012 survey, 71 percent of tree-fruit growers and almost 80 percent of raisin and berry growers said they were short of labor.
sentences.cn: 在2012年一项调查中，71%的果农和近80%的葡萄干和浆果种植者说他们缺少劳动力。

sentences.en: Some western farmers have responded by moving operations to Mexico.
sentences.cn: 一些西部农户则将生产转移至墨西哥以作应对。

sentences.en: From 1998 to 2000, 14.5 percent of the fruit Americans consumed was imported.
sentences.cn: 从1998年到2000年，美国人消费的水果中有14.5%是进口的。

sentences.en: Little more than a decade later, the share of imports was 25.8 percent.
sentences.cn: 仅仅十年后，进口占比为25.8%。

sentences.en: In effect, the U.S. can import food or it can import the workers who pick it.
sentences.cn: 实际上，美国可以进口食品，也可以进口采摘食品的工人。

sentences.en: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Dia Mirza and Adrian Grenier have a message for you: It's easy to beat plastic.
sentences.cn: 阿诺德·施瓦辛格，迪亚·莫扎和阿德里安·格兰尼想给你传递一条信息：战胜塑料轻而易举。

sentences.en: They're part of a bunch of celebrities starring in a new video for World Environment Day - encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples like straws and cutlery to combat the plastics crisis.
sentences.cn: 他们和一众明星主演了一部为世界环境日拍摄的新短片——鼓励你（消费者）换掉一次性塑料日用品，以对抗塑料危机。

sentences.en: The key messages that have been put together for World Environment Day do include a call for governments to enact legislation to curb single-use plastics.
sentences.cn: 在为宣传世界环境日而汇集的关键信息中，的确包括呼吁各政府制定法规以限制一次性塑料制品。

sentences.en: But the overarching message is directed at individuals.
sentences.cn: 但是，其中的核心信息是针对个人的。

sentences.en: My concern with leaving it up to the individual, however, is our limited sense of what needs to be achieved.
sentences.cn: 然而，对于将应对塑料危机的重任留给个人的做法，我的担忧在于人们对需要达成的目标认识有限。

sentences.en: On their own, taking our own bags to the grocery store or quitting plastic straws, for example, will accomplish little and require very little of us.
sentences.cn: 例如，仅仅提着自己的购物袋逛超市或停止使用塑料吸管，这种做法本身收效甚微，而且对人们提出的要求太低。

sentences.en: They could even be detrimental, satisfying a need to have "done our bit" without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions - a kind of "moral licensing" that allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.
sentences.cn: 它们甚至可能产生危害，满足人们“已尽本分”的（心理）需求，使人们不愿进一步采取更重大、更果敢、更有效的行动——这一“道德许可（效应）”会减轻人们的顾虑，让人们止步不前，不去做更多的事、对当权者提出更多的要求。

sentences.en: While the conversation around our environment and our responsibility toward it remains centered on shopping bags and straws, we're ignoring the balance of power that implies that as "consumers" we must shop sustainably, rather than as "citizens" hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change.
sentences.cn: 当围绕“我们的环境及我们对它的责任”这一讨论仍然聚焦于购物袋和吸管时，我们忽视了对一种力量的制衡，这股力量暗示，作为“消费者”我们必须可持续地消费，而不是以“公民”身份去追究政府和产业的责任以推动真正的系统性变革。

sentences.en: It's important to acknowledge that the environment isn't everyone's priority - or even most people's.
sentences.cn: 承认环境不是每个人——甚至不是多数人——优先考虑的事情，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: We shouldn't expect it to be.
sentences.cn: 我们也不应该指望它成为每个人的优先事项。

sentences.en: In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Wellesley College professor Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.
sentences.cn: 在其新作《为什么好人会做对环境有害的事》中，韦尔斯利学院教授伊丽莎白·R·德松布尔主张，集体改变大众行为的最佳方式是进行结构性改变。

sentences.en: This might mean implementing policy such as a plastic tax that adds a cost to environmentally problematic action, or banning single-use plastics altogether.
sentences.cn: 这可以是执行某项政策，比如对危害环境的行为增收一笔塑料税，或者完全禁止一次性塑料制品。

sentences.en: India has just announced it will "eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022."
sentences.cn: 印度刚刚宣布将“于2022年前消灭国内所有一次性塑料制品”。

sentences.en: There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.
sentences.cn: 此外，还有更便于人们作出更好的环保选择的激励式手段，比如确保回收利用至少同丢垃圾一样方便。

sentences.en: DeSombre isn't saying people should stop caring about the environment.
sentences.cn: 德松布尔并不是说人们不再需要关心环境。

sentences.en: It's just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior.
sentences.cn: 只是个体行动过于缓慢，她说，不足以成为改变某种普遍行为的唯一、乃至首要方法。

sentences.en: None of this is about writing off the individual.
sentences.cn: 这全无否定个体之意。

sentences.en: It's just about putting things into perspective.
sentences.cn: 不过是正确地认识形势。

sentences.en: We don't have time to wait.
sentences.cn: 我们没有时间去等。

sentences.en: We need progressive policies that shape collective action (and rein in polluting businesses), alongside engaged citizens pushing for change.
sentences.cn: 除了推动变革的积极公民，我们还需要影响集体行动的进步政策。

sentences.en: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid.
sentences.cn: 老鼠等动物必须要对同类发出的社交信号高度敏感，这样它们才能分辨哪些是可以合作的朋友，哪些是应该避开的敌人。

sentences.en: To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
sentences.cn: 为弄清这一敏感性在面对非生命体时是否仍适用，加州大学圣地亚哥分校的拉蕾·奎因及其同事进行了一项试验，观察老鼠是否能够感知机器鼠发出的社交信号。

sentences.en: They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat - one social and one asocial - for four days.
sentences.cn: 研究人员让8只成年鼠与2只不同类型的机器鼠——一只爱社交，一只不合群——共处一室4天。

sentences.en: The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
sentences.cn: 这两只机器鼠外形相当简约抽象，就像矮胖版的电脑鼠标，靠轮子四处移动，带有鲜艳的标记。

sentences.en: During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape.
sentences.cn: 在试验过程中，社交机器鼠跟随生物鼠们四处走动，玩同样的玩具，还会打开笼门让被困老鼠逃脱。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
sentences.cn: 在此期间，非社交机器鼠则只是前后、左右来回移动。

sentences.en: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.
sentences.cn: 接下来，研究人员将机器鼠关进笼子，并给老鼠一个按下控制杆解救机器鼠的机会。

sentences.en: Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one.
sentences.cn: 在对每只（生物鼠）各18次的试验中，生物鼠解救社交机器鼠的几率比解救非社交机器鼠的几率平均高出52%。

sentences.en: This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being.
sentences.cn: 这表明老鼠将社交机器鼠看作了真正的社交生物。

sentences.en: They may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing.
sentences.cn: 它们可能因先前社交机器鼠表现出集体探险及游戏等行为而与其建立了更强的情感纽带。

sentences.en: This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, says Quinn.
sentences.cn: 奎因称，这可能会使老鼠们更清楚记起自己之前曾经解救过机器鼠，并希望自己受困时能得到它相应的回报。

sentences.en: "Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity - where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them," says Quinn.
sentences.cn: “已有研究表明，老鼠会进行多种形式的互助及合作，其中包括被称为‘直接互惠’的行为，即老鼠会帮助之前曾帮助过自己的另一只老鼠。”奎因说道。

sentences.en: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.
sentences.cn: 出人意料的是，这只社交机器鼠设计如此简陋，老鼠却仍愿意与它交朋友。

sentences.en: The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels.
sentences.cn: 机器鼠虽与普通老鼠大小相当，外形却像一个带轮子的简易塑料盒。

sentences.en: "We'd assumed we'd have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn't necessary," says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
sentences.cn: “我们原以为必须给它加上活动的头和尾巴，面部特征和以假乱真的老鼠气味才行，但结果证明没有必要，”澳大利亚昆士兰大学的珍妮特·怀尔斯说道，她协助了此项研究。

sentences.en: The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots.
sentences.cn: 该发现表明老鼠对于社交信号非常敏感，即便这些信号来自简单的机器鼠。

sentences.en: Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals.
sentences.cn: 与之相似，儿童也往往将机器人视为同类，即便这些机器人只能发出简单的社交信号。

sentences.en: "We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too," says Wiles.
sentences.cn: “我们人类似乎被机器人深深吸引，事实证明其他动物也一样，”怀尔斯说道。

sentences.en: It is true that CEO pay has gone up - top ones may make 300 times the pay of typical workers on average, and since the mid-1970s, CEO pay for large publicly traded American corporations has, by varying estimates, gone up by about 500%.
sentences.cn: 的确，首席执行官（CEO）的薪酬上涨了——平均来看，顶级CEO的薪酬可能是普通员工薪酬的300倍，而且根据各种不同的估计，自上世纪70年代中期以来，美国大型上市公司的CEO薪酬上涨了约500%。

sentences.en: The typical CEO of a top American corporation now makes about $18.9 million a year.
sentences.cn: 美国顶级公司的典型CEO现在每年能挣到约1890万美元。

sentences.en: The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly.
sentences.cn: 理解CEO薪酬上涨的最佳模型是，全球顶级公司的商业机会在迅速增长，而CEO人才紧缺。

sentences.en: The efforts of America's highest-earning 1% have been one of the more dynamic elements of the global economy.
sentences.cn: 美国收入最高的1%人群的努力付出一直是全球经济的较强推动力之一。

sentences.en: It's not popular to say, but one reason their pay has gone up so much is that CEOs really have upped their game relative to many other workers in the U.S. economy.
sentences.cn: 尽管这么说不太讨喜，但CEO薪酬涨幅如此之大的一个原因是，相对于美国经济中的许多其他工作者来说，CEO确实提升了工作表现。

sentences.en: Today's CEO, at least for major American firms, must have many more skills than simply being able to "run the company."
sentences.cn: 如今的CEO，至少对于美国的大公司来说，必须拥有更多技能，而不仅仅是会“经营公司”而已。

sentences.en: CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them.
sentences.cn: CEO必须对金融市场有良好的判断力，甚至可能要熟知公司应该如何在这些市场中从事交易。

sentences.en: They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant.
sentences.cn: 相比前任们，他们还需要更厉害的公关能力，因为即使是一个小小的失误，也可能代价惨重。

sentences.en: Then there's the fact that large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries.
sentences.cn: 而且，美国大公司的全球化程度空前，供应链遍布更多的国家。

sentences.en: To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling.
sentences.cn: 要在这样的体系中发挥领导作用，必须有相当惊人的知识才行。

sentences.en: Plus, virtually all major American companies are becoming tech companies, often with their own research and development.
sentences.cn: 此外，几乎所有的美国大公司都在向科技公司转变，这些公司通常都要自主研发。

sentences.en: And beyond this, major CEOs still have to do all the day-to-day work they have always done.
sentences.cn: 除此之外，大CEO仍然要做他们一直在做的所有日常工作。

sentences.en: The common idea that high CEO pay is mainly about ripping people off doesn't explain history very well.
sentences.cn: 人们普遍认为CEO的高薪很大程度上是对员工的剥削，但这并不能很好地解释历史。

sentences.en: By most measures, corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s.
sentences.cn: 从大多数方面来看，公司治理自上世纪70年代以来大幅度收紧趋严。

sentences.en: Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising.
sentences.cn: 然而，CEO薪酬一直处于高位且持续上涨的趋势恰恰主要出现于强化治理的这段时期。

sentences.en: That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
sentences.cn: 这表明，招聘顶尖候选人从事日益艰难的工作符合公司的更广泛利益。

sentences.en: Furthermore, the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates, not to the cozy insider picks, another sign that high CEO pay is not some kind of depredation at the expense of the rest of the company.
sentences.cn: 此外，最高的CEO薪资是付给外部候选人的，而非付给那些安逸的内部人选，这也表明CEO高薪并不是某种以牺牲公司其他员工利益为代价的掠夺之举。

sentences.en: And the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO.
sentences.cn: 当公司将CEO薪酬与股价等因素挂钩时，股市会做出积极反应，这表明这些举措逐步增加公司价值，不仅仅是为了CEO。

sentences.en: Madrid was hailed as a public health guiding light last November when it rolled out ambitious restrictions on the most polluting cars.
sentences.cn: 去年十一月，马德里针对污染最严重的汽车正式推出大规模管控措施时，被誉为公共卫生健康的楷模。

sentences.en: Seven months and one election day later, a new conservative city council suspended enforcement of the clean air zone, a first step toward its possible termination.
sentences.cn: 七个月后大选日一过，由保守派掌控的新一届市议会随即中止了“清洁空气区”的执行，迈出了可能导致它被废除的第一步。

sentences.en: Mayor Jose Luis Martinez-Almeida made opposition to the zone a centrepiece of his election campaign, despite its success in improving air quality.
sentences.cn: 尽管“清洁空气区”在改善空气质量方面取得良好效果，但市长何塞·路易斯-马丁内斯-阿尔梅达却将反对它作为竞选运动的核心主张。

sentences.en: A judge has now overruled the city's decision to stop levying fines, ordering them restored.
sentences.cn: 目前，一名法官推翻了市政府停止收取罚金的决议，责令恢复收取罚金。

sentences.en: But with legal battles ahead, the zone's future looks uncertain at best.
sentences.cn: 但是，司法拉锯战在前，“清洁空气区”的未来充其量只能说是前途难卜。

sentences.en: Madrid's back and forth on clean air is a pointed reminder of the limits to the patchwork, city-by-city approach that characterises efforts on air pollution across Europe, Britain very much included.
sentences.cn: 马德里在清洁空气问题上的反反复复显而易见地提醒着我们，欧洲各国（当然也包括英国）这种零碎的市级空气污染治理举措的局限性。

sentences.en: Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically controversial, and therefore vulnerable.
sentences.cn: 各大城市独力承担污浊空气治理之责，其被迫不得已而采取的措施具有很多薄弱点，其中之一是：会引发政治争议，因而极易招致攻击。

sentences.en: That's because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers - who must pay fees or buy better vehicles - rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution.
sentences.cn: 这是因为，这些措施不可避免地将清洁空气的成本加诸司机个人——司机必须为污染付费或者买更好的车——而不是加诸汽车生产商，生产商的舞弊行为才是造成有毒污染的真正原因。

sentences.en: It's not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London.
sentences.cn: 不难想象，相似的逆转将在伦敦上演。

sentences.en: The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year's mayoral election.
sentences.cn: “超低排放新区（Ulez）”很可能是明年伦敦市长选举的重大议题。

sentences.en: And if Sadiq Khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
sentences.cn: 如果萨迪克·汗获胜，而且一如他所计划的那样于2021年将“超低排放新区”扩展至南北环路，那么一定会激起“届时将受影响的、数量大得多的汽车车主”的强烈反对。

sentences.en: It's not that measures such as London's Ulez are useless.
sentences.cn: 并不是说伦敦Ulez这类措施无用。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.cn: 恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents' health in the face of a serious threat.
sentences.cn: 严重威胁当前，地方官员正在运用他们所能使用的手段来保障居民健康。

sentences.en: The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits.
sentences.cn: 这些区域确实大大改善了空气质量，而且科学表明，空气质量改善意味着切实的健康收益。

sentences.en: But mayors and councilors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town.
sentences.cn: 但是，针对这么一个影响范围远超一城一镇的（空气污染）问题，市长们、议员们所能做的也就仅此而已。

sentences.en: They are acting because national governments - Britain's and others across Europe - have failed to do so.
sentences.cn: 他们之所以在行动，是因为各国政府——英国以及所有其他欧洲国家的政府——未能做出行动。

sentences.en: Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas - city centres, "school streets", even individual roads - are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance.
sentences.cn: 此类“禁止高污染汽车进入特定区域（如市中心、学区街道、甚至个别特殊道路）”的限制措施的出台，是因为“缺乏更大规模的行动以严格执行现有法规并要求汽车公司生产合规机动车”。

sentences.en: Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution.
sentences.cn: 威尔士公国现已推行特定低速限制以最小化污染。

sentences.en: We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
sentences.cn: 我们正在竭尽一切所能，却唯独没有坚决要求制造商“清洁”其汽车。

sentences.en: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring - the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year - the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks.
sentences.cn: 由于一些Z世代成员——对这代人最普遍接受的定义是出生于1995年之后（可有一年出入）——今春即将大学毕业，近几周对他们的关注也在不断增长。

sentences.en: Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades.
sentences.cn: Z世代即将涌入几十年来劳动力最为紧缺的职场，开启求职之旅。

sentences.en: And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U.S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers.
sentences.cn: 一项由美国大学和雇主协会开展的调查显示，在今年的美国，雇主计划比去年多雇佣约17%的应届毕业生。

sentences.en: Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
sentences.cn: 每个人都想知道，即将占据办公室空隔间的这些人与他们的前辈相比有何不同。

sentences.en: If "entitled" is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious.
sentences.cn: 如果“有权享有”是最常用于形容千禧一代（出生于1981至1995年间）的词——无论恰当与否——那么描述Z世代的关键词就是“讲求实际”和“谨慎小心”。

sentences.en: According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists.
sentences.cn: 据职业顾问和研究Z世代的专家称，Z世代是头脑清醒的经济实用主义者。

sentences.en: Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like.
sentences.cn: 尽管毕业于五十年来最好的经济形势，但Z世代了解经济火车失事的惨状。

sentences.en: They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both.
sentences.cn: 2008年经济崩盘时他们正是敏感的孩子，当时许多父母丢掉了工作或毕生积蓄，甚或二者一并丧失。

sentences.en: They aren't interested in taking any chances.
sentences.cn: 他们对冒险毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt.
sentences.cn: 蓬勃发展的经济似乎并未减轻这一代人深刻的忧患意识，对于那些背负大学债务的人尤其如此。

sentences.en: College loan balances in the U.S. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve.
sentences.cn: 根据美联储的数据，美国大学贷款欠额已达创纪录的1.5万亿美元。

sentences.en: One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind.
sentences.cn: 埃森哲咨询公司一项调查发现，今年毕业的大四学生中，88%在当初选择专业时已有心目中的工作。

sentences.en: In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose).
sentences.cn: 与此同时，佐治亚大学就业办公室在2019年一项针对该校学生的调查中发现，未来雇主最受欢迎的品质是提供稳定工作的能力（其后分别是职业发展及培训、激励人心的企业宗旨）。

sentences.en: Job security or stability was the second most important career goal (work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good.
sentences.cn: 工作保障或稳定是第二重要的职业目标（最重要的是“工作与生活平衡”），随后是事业奉献感或服务于宏大高尚事业的满足感。

sentences.en: That's a big change from the previous generation.
sentences.cn: 这和前一代人比起来是一个巨大转变。

sentences.en: "Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives," notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth.
sentences.cn: “千禧一代希望生活有更多的灵活性，”YouthSight副总监塔尼娅·米切尔森在可能同样适用于美国青年的调查发现中表示（YouthSight是英国一家品牌管理公司，每60天对英国青年展开定期调查）。

sentences.en: "Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy.
sentences.cn: “由于零工经济的崛起，Z世代寻求更多的确定性和稳定性。

sentences.en: They have trouble seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse."
sentences.cn: 他们难以看到经济前景，极力规避风险。”

sentences.en: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind.
sentences.cn: “再培训”虽然听上去像个时髦词，但实际上，如果我们希望未来的劳动力不被大量抛弃，那它就是一件必须要做的事情。

sentences.en: We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain.
sentences.cn: 众所周知，我们正步入这样一个时期：（社会）所需的工作岗位将迅速变化，而剩余工作岗位的要求也将迅速变化。

sentences.en: Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022.
sentences.cn: 世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，各类职业中平均42%的“核心技能”将发生变化。

sentences.en: That is a very short timeline.
sentences.cn: 这是非常短的时间。

sentences.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one.
sentences.cn: “谁该为再培训付费”是一个棘手的问题。

sentences.en: For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are.
sentences.cn: 对各公司来说，解雇技能过时的员工，用掌握紧缺技能的人取而代之，这一直是个有吸引力的办法。

sentences.en: That does not always happen.
sentences.cn: 当然，这也并非必然。

sentences.en: AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy.
sentences.cn: 美国电话电报公司（AT&T）便常常被奉为（反其道而行之的）完美范例，该公司采用了大规模的技能再培训方案，而非“先裁后聘”的策略。

sentences.en: Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans.
sentences.cn: 其他包括亚马逊和迪士尼在内的公司也已承诺会制定各自的方案。

sentences.en: When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle.
sentences.cn: 不过，在更宏观的经济层面看待技能不匹配这一现象时，人们往往将焦点投向政府，希望由其来解决这一问题。

sentences.en: Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
sentences.cn: 当前，加拿大及其他地方所作的努力充其量只能说是迟缓无力的，结果造成了这样一个局面：即便是在高失业率时期和地区，我们也经常听到雇主急缺员工。

sentences.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed.
sentences.cn: 由于疫情，失业率的确居高不下。

sentences.en: In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.
sentences.cn: 二月份，加拿大和美国的失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%，处于近二三十年低点，员工短缺问题遍布各地。

sentences.en: As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so.
sentences.cn: 到了五月，两国的失业率飙升至13.3%和13.7%。尽管许多员工短缺问题已不复存在，但并非都是如此。

sentences.en: In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
sentences.cn: 举个显而易见的例子，在医疗领域，疫情表明医生、护士以及其他医务人员仍然处于明显短缺状态。

sentences.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it.
sentences.cn: 当然，这并不是说我们可以找来一个失业的服务员，不管谁来为此付钱，在几周内把他培训成医生。

sentences.en: But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.
sentences.cn: 但是，即使不能弥合这个缺口，我们或许可以弥合其他缺口，这样做将对相关各方都有利。

sentences.en: That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff.
sentences.cn: 瑞典的情况似乎就是如此：北欧航空公司90%的空乘人员被迫休假后，该公司决定启动一项短期再培训方案，重新培训下岗员工来支援医护人员。

sentences.en: The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
sentences.cn: 这是一项集体行动，其他公司以及一所瑞典大学也参与其中。

sentences.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.
sentences.cn: 预计到2050年，全球人口将多达近100亿，预测若要跟上步伐，某些地区的农业产量需接近翻倍，因此，粮食保障问题正越来越多地占据头条新闻。

sentences.en: In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
sentences.cn: 在英国，它最近也成了重大议题，原因相当独特：脱欧。

sentences.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food.
sentences.cn: 脱欧被一些人视为扭转“英国粮食进口”这一新近趋势的契机。

sentences.en: The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s.
sentences.cn: 上世纪80年代末，英国生产的粮食占其食用总量的近3/4，而现在则下滑到了仅60%。

sentences.en: A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health.
sentences.cn: 这些人的观点为，恢复自给自足将会促进农业发展、加强政治主权，甚至提升国民健康。

sentences.en: Sounds great - but how feasible is this vision?
sentences.cn: 听起来很棒——但这一愿景的可行性如何？

sentences.en: According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production.
sentences.cn: 英国利兹大学关于“英国粮食生产”的报告中指出，英国土地总面积的85%与肉类及奶制品的生产相关联。

sentences.en: That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
sentences.cn: 这供应了英国所消费食物的80%，所以即便让畜牧场覆盖全国，也无法满足我们全部的肉类及奶制品需求。

sentences.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave.
sentences.cn: 虽然有许多就这些数据局限性的提醒，但它们所反映的形势仍旧严峻。

sentences.en: To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively - meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
sentences.cn: 英国若想大幅提高自给率，就要急剧减少食用动物性食品，并且或许还需要更集约地从事农业活动——这意味着绿色原野减少、工厂式生产增加。

sentences.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help.
sentences.cn: 但转向以植物为主的饮食也不会有太大意义。

sentences.en: There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis.
sentences.cn: 英国畜牧业占大头是有充分理由的：它的大部分地带都不具备适宜商业化种植的土壤和气候。

sentences.en: Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
sentences.cn: 全国只有25%的土地适合作物栽培，而且其中大部分都已经成为耕地了。

sentences.en: Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg - which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes - we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
sentences.cn: 就算我们把所有条件适宜的土地都变成果蔬园地——这会牵扯到取消所有的自然保护区以及让成千上万的人们搬离家园——我们能实现的粮食产量增长也只有30%而已。

sentences.en: Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs.
sentences.cn: 如今英国人食用的果蔬中仅有23%产自本国，所以，哪怕采用最极端的手段，我们也只能满足鲜果蔬需求的30%。

sentences.en: That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
sentences.cn: 而在此之后，我们还得再找地方来种植谷物、糖类、籽类、油类等，它们提供了我们当前摄入的大部分卡路里。

sentences.en: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.
sentences.cn: 2015年，微软收购任务管理应用Wunderlist和移动日历Sunrise时，挑选的是当时在硅谷名声大噪的两家新科技公司。

sentences.en: Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for "productivity" software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
sentences.cn: 微软自创的Office在“生产效率”软件市场独占鳌头，而这两家初创企业则代表了智能手机领域全新科技的一股新潮。

sentences.en: Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.
sentences.cn: 然而，这两款应用后来都被下架了，微软表示已将其最佳性能融入到了自身产品中。

sentences.en: Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many "acqui-hires" that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
sentences.cn: 两款应用的工程师团队留了下来，使之成为大型科技公司为弥补科技人才紧缺而进行的众多“人才并购”的两例。

sentences.en: To Microsoft's critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
sentences.cn: 在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist和Sunrise的命运表明：科技巨头会无情地蚕食一切阻碍其发展的创新公司。

sentences.en: "They bought the seedlings and closed them down," complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.
sentences.cn: 总部位于旧金山的Switch风险投资公司合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨道，“他们买下这些初创企业然后将其关闭”，将那些有朝一日可能会成长为竞争对手的企业扼杀于摇篮。

sentences.en: Microsoft declined to comment.
sentences.cn: 微软拒绝对此置评。

sentences.en: Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: "I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.
sentences.cn: 和其他初创企业投资者一样，阿诺德的公司也常常依赖于将初创企业出售给大型科技公司，不过对于收购结局他内心五味杂陈：“自私一点说，我认为这些收购对我有利。

sentences.en: But are they good for the American economy?
sentences.cn: 但它们对美国经济有利吗？

sentences.en: I don't know."
sentences.cn: 我不知道。”

sentences.en: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.
sentences.cn: 美国联邦贸易委员会表示希望找到这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
sentences.cn: 本周，委员会要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年内进行的诸多小型收购的相关信息。

sentences.en: Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
sentences.cn: 尽管在现阶段这项要求只是一个研究项目，却让人们燃起了希望：监管机构开始介入此前不曾涉足的早期科技市场。

sentences.en: Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals - many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise - might seem beside the point.
sentences.cn: 鉴于这五家科技公司的总市值超过5.5万亿美元，匆忙审查这些小额收购（其中许多远没有Wunderlist、Sunrise收购案引人注目）似乎有些避重就轻的味道。

sentences.en: Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years - a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
sentences.cn: 过去的五年中，这五大科技公司加起来平均每年只花34亿美元用于10亿美元以下的收购。这个数额同他们庞大的资金储备以及去年在美国完成的1300多亿美元的风险投资相比，无异于沧海一粟。

sentences.en: However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a "buy and kill" tactic to simply close them down.
sentences.cn: 但批评人士认为，这些大公司利用这样的交易，在最具危险性的潜在竞争对手有机会形成势头之前将他们买下，有些时候就是“买了即杀”策略中的一步，就是要让他们关门。

sentences.en: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.
sentences.cn: 我们很擅长运用第一印象——“经验薄片”来评判他人（从对照片的一瞥，到长达五分钟的互动都可称为“经验薄片”），此时深思不仅没有必要，而且会造成干扰。

sentences.en: In one study of the ability she called "thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness.
sentences.cn: 在纳里尼·安巴迪称为“行为薄片撷取”能力的一项研究中，这位已故的心理学家要求参与者观看教授们（授课）的10秒无声视频片段，并对教师的整体效果进行评分。

sentences.en: Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings.
sentences.cn: 他们的评分与学生在学期末（对教师）的评分高度相关。

sentences.en: Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.
sentences.cn: 另一组参与者在观看视频片段时需要从1000开始以9为单位倒数，这占用了他们的意识工作记忆。

sentences.en: Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
sentences.cn: 这组人的评分也同样准确，这显示出“社会信息处理”的直觉性。

sentences.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.
sentences.cn: 极为关键的是，另一组参与者被要求在评分之前花一分钟写下他们做出判断的原因。

sentences.en: Accuracy dropped dramatically.
sentences.cn: 此时，评分的准确性大幅下降。

sentences.en: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
sentences.cn: 安巴迪推测，深思使参与者将精力集中于那些生动但具有误导性的信号（比如特定的手势或说话方式），而未能让微妙信号间的复杂关系形成整体印象。

sentences.en: She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
sentences.cn: 她发现，参与者在观看15秒的双人视频片段，然后判断两者是陌生人、朋友还是约会对象时，也会受到类似的干扰。

sentences.en: Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection.
sentences.cn: 其他研究表明，我们在依靠直觉而非深思时，更能从“行为薄片”中察觉出欺骗。

sentences.en: "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing.
sentences.cn: “这就像你在开手动挡汽车，”东北大学心理学家朱迪斯·霍尔说，“如果你开始反复思考如何挂挡，你就会忘记自己本来是要做什么。

sentences.en: But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine.
sentences.cn: 但如果你不假思索地按照习惯操作，就不会遇到什么问题。

sentences.en: Much of our social life is like that."
sentences.cn: 我们的社交生活也多半如此。”

sentences.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.
sentences.cn: 考虑得过多也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。

sentences.en: College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale.
sentences.cn: 在不要求大学生细察其依据的情况下，他们对草莓果酱和大学课程的评估与专家的意见更一致。

sentences.en: And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex - when they had a lot of information to process.
sentences.cn: 而在人们被要求关注感受而非细节时，做出的购车决定会在客观上更合适，而且更令自己满意，但也只有在这一决定很复杂的情况下方才如此——（因为）此时人们有很多信息要处理。

sentences.en: Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.
sentences.cn: 直觉的特殊能力只有在特定的情境下才会发挥出来。

sentences.en: In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).
sentences.cn: 在一项研究中，参与者完成了一组八项任务，其中四项运用了深度思索能力（辨识规则、理解词汇），另外四项运用了直觉与创造力（创造新产品或修辞格）。

sentences.en: Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," "hunches," "my heart").
sentences.cn: 而后，他们对自己使用直觉（“本能”“预感”“内心”）的程度给出了评分。

sentences.en: Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
sentences.cn: 不出所料，使用直觉损害了他们在前四项任务中的表现，而对其余的任务则有所帮助。

sentences.en: Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
sentences.cn: 有时候，心比脑更聪明。

sentences.en: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown's 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas.
sentences.cn: 不久前的一天，艳阳高照，一万三千只鸡在拉里·布朗位于得克萨斯州希纳市的40英亩向风的露天农场里自由活动着。

sentences.en: Some rest in the shade of a parked car.
sentences.cn: 一些在一辆停放着的汽车的阴影处休息。

sentences.en: Others drink water with the cows.
sentences.cn: 另一些在和奶牛们一起喝水。

sentences.en: This all seems random, but it's by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.
sentences.cn: 这一切看起来散漫无序，但却是刻意使然，其背后反映了61亿美元规模的美国蛋品行业所押注的下一个行业风口：气候友好型鸡蛋。

sentences.en: These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they're also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture - special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap green-house gases.
sentences.cn: 目前这类鸡蛋正首次上架，售价高达8美元一打，它们依旧被标注为“有机”“动物友好型”，但生产这类鸡蛋的禽类养殖农场此外还运用了再生农业——用于培育可捕获温室气体的肥沃土壤的专项技术。

sentences.en: Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.
sentences.cn: 像这样生产出来的鸡蛋可以被营销成有助于对抗气候变化的产品。

sentences.en: "I'm excited about our progress," says Brown, who is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat.
sentences.cn: “我对我们取得的进步感到兴奋。”布朗说道。他正在种植更多覆土作物以招引蠕虫和蟋蟀给鸡吃。

sentences.en: The birds' waste then fertilizes fields.
sentences.cn: 鸡粪又可以肥沃田地。

sentences.en: Such improvements "allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers."
sentences.cn: 这些改进做法“让我们的母鸡能够自主搜寻更优质的天然饲料，这种饲料对土壤、母鸡以及我们供应给客户的鸡蛋都会有好处。”

sentences.en: The egg industry's push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering.
sentences.cn: 蛋品行业（对再生鸡蛋）的营销是检验再生农场动物产品能否成为下一个优质品类的首个重要试金石。

sentences.en: In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart.
sentences.cn: 在短短十多年的时间里，有机鸡蛋从天然食品店里无人问津的小众产品变成了沃尔玛大卖场的商品。

sentences.en: More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories.
sentences.cn: 就在不久前，人们对益生菌食品和植物肉也同样抱有怀疑态度，但如今这两类食品都已成为超市的重要品类。

sentences.en: If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
sentences.cn: 如果可持续鸡蛋成功推向市场，这有可能会为再生牛肉、再生西兰花以及更多的再生产品打开市场闸门。

sentences.en: Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine.
sentences.cn: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学布兰迪万分校的农业经济学副教授朱莉·斯坦顿说，再生产品可能很难被市场接受，因为这个概念很难用三言两语解释清楚。

sentences.en: Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products (though some producers say their eggs have more protein).
sentences.cn: 这种农业生产方式对食用农产品起到的改良作用也是微乎其微，甚至为零（尽管一些生产商说他们的鸡蛋含有更多的蛋白质）。

sentences.en: The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability.
sentences.cn: 该行业正押注打赌：那些花更多钱为“自由放养”“非转基因”“牧场饲养鸡蛋”等优质产品特性买单的消费者同样会乐意接受“可持续性”概念。

sentences.en: Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment.
sentences.cn: 调查显示，年轻一代更关心气候变化，植物肉的成功就可部分归因于购物者想要表达保护环境的愿望。

sentences.en: Young adults "really care about the planet," says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations.
sentences.cn: Egg Innovations公司的总裁约翰·布伦克尔指出，年轻人“真的很关心地球。

sentences.en: "They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even they understand what they're doing."
sentences.cn: 毫无疑问，他们正在改变食品供应链，我觉得甚至他们自己都不知道这一点。”

sentences.en: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
sentences.cn: 越来越多的美国人选择退休后继续工作，这一增长趋势可能会颠覆旧有的劳动力模式。

sentences.en: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have, or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
sentences.cn: 根据哈里斯民意调查公司（Harris Poll）为德美利证券公司（TD Ameritrade）进行的一项调查，40岁及以上的美国人中，有三分之一已经或计划在退休后继续工作，以为更长远的人生做准备。

sentences.en: Even more surprising is that more than half of "unretirees" - those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring - said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
sentences.cn: 更出人意料的是，调查显示，超过一半的“不退休者”（即打算退休后继续工作，或退休后已重返工作岗位的人）称，即便他们有足够的钱安稳度日，他们也愿意在晚年再就业。

sentences.en: Financial needs aren't the only culprit for the "unretirement" trend.
sentences.cn: 财务需求并非引发“不退休”潮流的唯一原因。

sentences.en: Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression.
sentences.cn: 根据该研究，其他原因还包括“个人满足感”，例如保持心理健康，防止无聊或避免抑郁等。

sentences.en: "The concept of retirement is evolving," said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade.
sentences.cn: “退休观念正在逐渐改变。”德美利证券公司退休事务部高级经理克里斯汀·罗素说，

sentences.en: "It's not just about finances.
sentences.cn: “它不仅关乎财务状况，

sentences.en: The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement."
sentences.cn: 工作的益处也驱使着人们退休后继续工作。”

sentences.en: One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer.
sentences.cn: 退休模式转变的一个原因是美国人的寿命越来越长。

sentences.en: Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the U.S. workforce.
sentences.cn: 在美国，老年人也是劳动力中增长最快的群体。

sentences.en: The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades.
sentences.cn: 过去三十年来，退休年龄人口在劳动力中的比例翻了一番。

sentences.en: About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February 2019, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
sentences.cn: 根据资金管理公司United Income的数据，2019年2月，65岁及以上人口占劳动力的比例已从1985年1月10%的历史最低水平增至约20%。

sentences.en: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2,000 adults between 40 to 79.
sentences.cn: 德美利证券公司的该项研究对2000名40～79岁的成人进行了调查，结果显示，由于寿命延长，美国人也在增加储蓄以留存养老储备金。

sentences.en: Six in 10 "unretirees" are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life.
sentences.cn: 有五分之三的“不退休者”预见到寿命延长，选择增加储蓄。

sentences.en: Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.
sentences.cn: 该公司称，这些人最常用的方法是减少总体开支、购买人寿保险或尽可能多缴纳退休金。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
sentences.cn: 总部位于巴尔的摩的财务规划公司Facet Wealth的联合创始人布伦特·韦斯指出，遗憾的是，许多选择在退休后工作的人之所以准备这样做，是因为他们担心晚年的生计问题。

sentences.en: He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
sentences.cn: 他建议，尚未退休的人应该咨询财务顾问，设定长期的财务目标。

sentences.en: "The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring," Weiss said.
sentences.cn: “人生中最具挑战性的时刻是结婚、组建家庭以及最终退休。”韦斯说道，

sentences.en: "It's not just a financial decision, but an emotional one.
sentences.cn: “退休不仅是个财务决定，也是个情感决定。

sentences.en: Many people believe they can't retire."
sentences.cn: 许多人都认为他们不能退休。”

sentences.en: We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives.
sentences.cn: 无论在个人生活还是职场生活中，我们都遇到过这种情况。

sentences.en: Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel.
sentences.cn: 想想那些自己感到受骗或懊恼的时刻：某会员身份或订阅服务注册过程流畅无缝，随后取消却极其困难。

sentences.en: Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice.
sentences.cn: 一些本应简单易懂的事物可能会在有意或无意之间变得复杂难懂，从而损害消费者的选择权。

sentences.en: These are examples of dark patterns.
sentences.cn: 这些都是黑暗模式的例子。

sentences.en: First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, "dark patterns" is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users.
sentences.cn: 2010年由用户体验专家哈里·布努首创的“黑暗模式”这一术语是对“操纵用户界面，以影响用户决策能力”做法的统称。

sentences.en: Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to "roach motel," where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.
sentences.cn: 布努发现了12种常见的黑暗模式，从误导、隐藏成本到“蟑螂汽车旅馆”，在这些模式下，开始时用户体验看似简单便捷，而当用户试图退出时就会变得非常困难。

sentences.en: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices.
sentences.cn: 在2019年一项涵盖5.3万个产品页面和1.1万个网站的研究中，研究人员发现大约有十分之一的页面或网站运用了这些设计手法。

sentences.en: Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood.
sentences.cn: 黑暗模式尽管盛行，但其概念仍未被充分了解。

sentences.en: Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.
sentences.cn: 企业及非营利组织的领导者们应该了解黑暗模式并尽量避开它们生成的灰色区域。

sentences.en: Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns?
sentences.cn: “合乎道德又有诱惑力的设计”和“黑暗模式”之间的界限在哪里？

sentences.en: Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company's user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions.
sentences.cn: 企业应与IT团队、合规团队、风险团队及法律团队进行对话，审查自己的隐私政策，并让以下人员参与讨论：负责公司用户界面的客户/用户体验设计师和编码员，以及负责注册、结账篮、定价、促销的营销者和广告商。

sentences.en: Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding "digital deception."
sentences.cn: 上述团队无论是任何一个还是全部一起，都能在无论是制造还是避免“数字欺诈”方面发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level.
sentences.cn: 立法者和监管者正慢慢开始设法厘清黑暗模式相关法律的模糊之处，其最近行动开展于州级层面。

sentences.en: In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that "ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights."
sentences.cn: 今年3月，加州司法部长宣布批准了《加州消费者隐私法案》（CCPA）补充规定，这些规定将“确保消费者在寻求行使数据隐私权时不会被迷惑或误导”。

sentences.en: The regulations aim to ban dark patterns - this means prohibiting companies from using confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn't opt out."
sentences.cn: 这些规定旨在禁止黑暗模式——这意味着严禁公司使用“令人费解的语言或不必要的步骤，如强迫用户点击多个页面或听取不应选择退出的理由”。

sentences.en: As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community.
sentences.cn: 随着越来越多的州考虑颁布补充规定，商界内部需要增强责任感。

sentences.en: Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.
sentences.cn: 黑暗模式也可以在自我监管的基础上得以解决，但前提是各机构自己担负起责任，不仅要对法律要求负责，还要对行业最佳实践和最高标准负责。

sentences.en: Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports.
sentences.cn: 尽管道德课在世界各地都很普遍，但科学家们尚不确定这些课程是否真能改变行为：正反两方面的证据都很薄弱，它们依赖的是人为的实验室试验，有时候（甚至）是不可靠的自陈报告。

sentences.en: But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.
sentences.cn: 但一项发表在《认知》杂志上的新研究发现，仅一节道德课就可能产生了持久的影响，至少在一种现实情形中是如此。

sentences.en: The researchers investigated one class session's impact on eating meat.
sentences.cn: 研究人员调查了一堂（道德）课对吃肉行为的影响。

sentences.en: They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students' attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering.
sentences.cn: 研究报告的合著者、加州大学河滨分校的哲学家埃里克·施维茨格贝尔表示，他们选择这种特定行为的原因有三：学生对吃肉的看法多变且不稳定，吃肉行为很容易衡量，道德文献大多认为少吃肉有益，因为这样能减少对环境的危害以及给动物的痛苦。

sentences.en: Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory-farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion.
sentences.cn: 在四个大哲学班里，一半学生阅读了一篇有关工厂化肉类养殖的伦理文章，非强制性观看了一段有关少吃肉的11分钟的视频，并开展了50分钟的讨论。

sentences.en: The other half focused on charitable giving instead.
sentences.cn: 另一半学生则关注的是慈善捐赠这一话题。

sentences.en: Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester - nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students.
sentences.cn: 然后，在学生们不知情的情况下，研究人员仔细研究了这一学期的餐卡匿名消费情况——近500名学生的近14000张消费小票。

sentences.en: Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books.
sentences.cn: 施维茨格贝尔之前预测，这种干预行为不会产生任何影响；（因为）此前他就已发现，伦理学教授在投票率、献血以及归还馆藏图书等一系列行为上跟其他的教授们并无二致。

sentences.en: But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent - and this effect held steady for the study's duration of several weeks.
sentences.cn: 但是，在参与探讨肉食伦理的学生受试人群中，肉餐购买比率从52%下降到45%——而且这一影响在研究持续的几周内一直保持平稳。

sentences.en: Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.
sentences.cn: 另一组学生的肉餐购买比率则一直保持在52%不变。

sentences.en: "That's actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention," Schwitzgebel says.
sentences.cn: 施维茨格贝尔说：“对一个极小的干预行为来说，这的确是一个极大的影响。”

sentences.en: Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable.
sentences.cn: 没有参与这项研究的宾夕法尼亚大学的心理学家尼娜·施特罗明格指出，她希望这个影响是真实的，但并不能排除（存在）某个未知的混杂变量。

sentences.en: And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: "Easy come, easy go."
sentences.cn: 她特别提到，这种影响即便是真实的，也可能会因另一个微小的外力而被逆转：“来得快，去得也快。”

sentences.en: Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence - classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common.
sentences.cn: 施维茨格贝尔觉得最大的影响来自社交影响——主导讨论走向的同学或助教可能分享了自己的素食主义，表明了它的可行性或者常见性。

sentences.en: Second, the video may have had an emotional impact.
sentences.cn: 其次，视频可能也造成了情绪感染。

sentences.en: Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role.
sentences.cn: 他认为，理性讨论的影响是最小的，不过他的合著者却认为，理性发挥的作用可能更大。

sentences.en: Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants' eating habits and students' video exposure.
sentences.cn: 现在，研究人员正在探索教学风格、助教的饮食习惯和学生观看视频的具体影响。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Schwitzgebel - who had predicted no effect - will be eating his words.
sentences.cn: 而与此同时，预测不会产生任何影响的施维茨格贝尔也将收回前言。

sentences.en: In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut—and it is the environment that is paying the price.
sentences.cn: 全国各地的房主都在为追求完美草坪而走捷径——而为此付出代价的却是环境。

sentences.en: About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles.
sentences.cn: 每年大约有800万平方米的塑料草坪售出，而反对（塑料草坪）的声音现已蔓延至最高园艺界。

sentences.en: The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year's event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos.
sentences.cn: 切尔西花展已禁止在今年的活动中使用人造草坪，并宣称使用人造草坪不符合其活动理念。

sentences.en: The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.
sentences.cn: 在伦敦西区举办该年度展会的皇家园艺协会表示，之所以实施这项禁令，是因为塑料草坪会对环境和生物多样性造成破坏。

sentences.en: Ed Horne, of the RHS, said: "We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic.
sentences.cn: 皇家园艺协会的埃德·霍恩表示：“我们去年推出了可持续发展战略，而使用人造草坪与我们的理念以及我们对塑料的看法背道而驰。

sentences.en: We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment."
sentences.cn: 我们建议使用天然草坪，因为它会带来诸多环境效益，包括维持野生动物生存、减轻洪涝灾害以及给环境‘降温’。”

sentences.en: The RHS's decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes.
sentences.cn: 皇家园艺协会做出这一决定之际，活动人士正努力提高人们对人造草坪所造成问题的认识。

sentences.en: A Twitter account, which claims to "cut through the greenwash" of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers.
sentences.cn: 一个推特账户声称要“刺穿人造草坪的‘绿色外衣’”，目前已获得2万多人关注。

sentences.en: It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an "ecological damage" tax on such lawns.
sentences.cn: 该账户力劝人们签署两份请愿书，其中一份呼吁禁止销售塑料草坪，另一份则呼吁对此类草坪征收“生态破坏”税。

sentences.en: They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.
sentences.cn: 两份请愿书已分别收集到7276个和11282个签名。

sentences.en: However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol.
sentences.cn: 然而，人造草坪的支持者表示，天然草坪需要修剪，因此通常会耗电耗油，也会对环境造成影响。

sentences.en: The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more.
sentences.cn: 该行业同样指出，天然草坪需要喷洒大量的水和除草剂，还需要其他诸多养护工作，而铺设人造草坪的人往往会更经常使用其花园。

sentences.en: The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.
sentences.cn: 该行业还声称，铺设人造草坪的人平均会花费500英镑在花园的树木或灌木上，而这为昆虫提供了栖息之所。

sentences.en: In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has "no plans to ban the use of artificial grass".
sentences.cn: 去年另一份要求禁止人造草坪的请愿书获得了3万人签名，对此政府回应道，其“并不打算禁止人造草坪的使用”。

sentences.en: It added: "We prefer to help people and organisations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters.
sentences.cn: 它补充道：“我们更愿帮助公众及相关组织做出正确的选择，而不是就此问题立法。

sentences.en: However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives."
sentences.cn: 不过，人造草坪的使用必须遵守现有的法律和政策的保障措施，以保护生物多样性，确保排水的可持续性，而诸如加强生物多样性责任的措施，应该有助于鼓励公共当局考虑可持续的替代方案。”

sentences.en: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks.
sentences.cn: 联邦政府填补国家公园长期存在的资金缺口的想法很容易被视为荒唐可笑而不予考虑。

sentences.en: Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?
sentences.cn: 难道真的有人会认为，允许亚马逊把货送到约塞米蒂国家公园的帐篷里或允许食品卡车在（加州）红杉国家公园的红杉树下排队是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis.
sentences.cn: 但有一点政府是对的：美国国家公园正处于危机之中。

sentences.en: Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion.
sentences.cn: 总的来说，它们所积压的维护费用超过120亿美元。

sentences.en: Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.
sentences.cn: 车行道、步行道、卫生间、游客中心和其他基础设施都在日渐破败。

sentences.en: But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all.
sentences.cn: 然而，将露营地私有化、商业化并非万能之计。

sentences.en: Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.
sentences.cn: 露营地只占全部基础设施维护积压工作的极小部分，而且（入驻）公园的商家平均只向国家公园管理局上缴约5%的收入。

sentences.en: Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.
sentences.cn: 此外，（露营地的）进一步私有化必定会削弱每年3亿游客游园的一个主要诱因：享受自然，从淹没日常生活的商业喧嚣中小憩片刻。

sentences.en: The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding.
sentences.cn: 真正的问题在于国家公园长期缺乏资金。

sentences.en: An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact.
sentences.cn: 一项针对700名美国纳税人的经济调查发现，人们愿意支付一大笔钱，以确保国家公园及其项目保持完好无损。

sentences.en: Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.
sentences.cn: 约81%的受访者表示，他们愿意在未来10年内支付额外的税费，以避免对国家公园的任何削减。

sentences.en: The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature.
sentences.cn: 国家公园作为隐逸的去处以及自然的象征，为美国居民提供了巨大价值。

sentences.en: On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism.
sentences.cn: 除此之外，国家公园也创造价值，它们开展各种各样的教育项目，通过“碳封存”对气候产生积极影响，同时为我们的文化和艺术生活做出贡献，当然还发展旅游业。

sentences.en: The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life.
sentences.cn: 国家公园还有助于让美国的历史保持“活力”，它们与全国数千个地方辖区合作，以保护历史遗迹，让这些地方的故事鲜活起来。

sentences.en: The parks do all this on a shoestring.
sentences.cn: 国家公园靠着微薄的资金做着所有这一切。

sentences.en: Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009.
sentences.cn: 国会每年仅向国家公园系统拨款30亿美元，这一数额自2001年以来一直持平（按通货膨胀调整后的美元计算），除2009年提振一次以外。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.
sentences.cn: 相比之下，自1980年以来，每年的游客人数增长50%以上，现如今每年高达3.3亿人次。

sentences.en: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow.
sentences.cn: 哥伦比亚大学心理学教授贝齐·斯帕罗表示，互联网可能只是改变了我们的记忆内容，而并未改变我们的记忆能力。

sentences.en: In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer ("an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain," for example).
sentences.cn: 2011年，斯帕罗主持了一项研究，参与者被要求在电脑中记录40条有趣信息（例如“鸵鸟的眼睛比它的大脑大”）。

sentences.en: Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved.
sentences.cn: 一半的参与者被告知这些信息将会被删除，而另一半则被告知信息会被保存。

sentences.en: Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers.
sentences.cn: 你猜怎么着？后一组参与者在随后的测验中丝毫不做努力来回忆这些信息，因为他们知道可以在电脑上找到这些信息。

sentences.en: In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in.
sentences.cn: 也是在这项研究中，一组参与者被要求同时记住信息和存放信息的文件夹。

sentences.en: They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders.
sentences.cn: 他们没有记住信息本身，但记得如何找到文件夹。

sentences.en: In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but "adapting to new communications technology," Sparrow says.
sentences.cn: 换句话说，人类的记忆不是在退化，而是在“适应新的通信技术”，斯帕罗说。

sentences.en: In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as "cognitive offloading."
sentences.cn: 互联网正在以一种非常切实有效的方式成为存储我们记忆的外部硬盘，这个过程被称为“认知卸载”。

sentences.en: Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans.
sentences.cn: 传统上，这个角色是由数据库、图书馆和他人来扮演的。

sentences.en: Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance.
sentences.cn: 例如，你的父亲可能从来不记得你们的生日，因为你的母亲记得。

sentences.en: Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside.
sentences.cn: 有些人担心这一过程正在对社会产生破坏性的影响，但斯帕罗看到了积极的一面。

sentences.en: Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet.
sentences.cn: 她认为，也许这一趋势将使得我们的学习方式从关注个别事实和死记硬背转变为强调更多的概念性思考——这是互联网所不具备的事物。

sentences.en: "I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things," Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it.
sentences.cn: “我个人从来不认为死记硬背有那么大的智力价值，”斯帕罗说，并补充指出我们并未失去这样做（即对……进行死记硬背）的能力。

sentences.en: Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains.
sentences.cn: 不过，其他一些专家认为，现在要了解互联网如何影响我们的大脑还为时过早。

sentences.en: There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons.
sentences.cn: 比如，心理学家克里斯托弗·查布里斯和丹尼尔·J.西蒙斯写道，目前没有实验证据表明互联网会干扰我们的专注能力。

sentences.en: And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.
sentences.cn: 而且，2008年加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔神经科学和人类行为研究所开展的一项涉及24名参与者的研究显示，在精通电脑的老年人中，浏览网页比阅读更能锻炼大脑。
